doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Self-taught arranging, writing for players like Ellington
summary: He had no formal arranging lessons and writes for the players' concepts, as Ellington did.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Were you getting a sense of maybe later on some of that experience when you started composing went back to those days when you were playing with saxophone players and getting an idea of how to orchestrate and arrange. Did you ever have formal lessons in that?

No. You know I’m self taught at that. So you know I know what I hear when I write music for the players and their concepts like Duke Ellington did, he used to write for all the personalities in his orchestra you know. So he wrote that way so the composition would bring the most out of the player, you know, and that that would be a reciprocal exchange in the dialogue, the musical dialogue.
